files.README.md:
# Umami

Privacy-friendly web analytics with a Postgres database. The dashboard is behind the SlicedBread login wall; the tracker script and event endpoint are public. An install action replaces Umami's default admin password with a generated one.
files.actions/dashboard-login.mjs:
#!/usr/bin/env node
console.log(JSON.stringify({ url: process.env.SB_APP_URL, username: "admin", password: process.env.UMAMI_ADMIN_PASSWORD }));

files.README.md:
# Vaultwarden

Bitwarden-compatible password manager. Registration is team-only: the registration endpoints pass the SlicedBread login wall, the rest of the app does not, so Bitwarden apps and extensions log in directly. The setup step "Create your account" disappears once an account exists.
files.template.yaml:
apiVersion: bakery.slicedbread.dev/v1
name: vaultwarden
version: 1.1.0
description: Password manager compatible with Bitwarden apps and browser extensions.
upstream: {project: Vaultwarden, url: https://github.com/dani-garcia/vaultwarden, licence: AGPL-3.0}
access:
  mode: app-auth               # Bitwarden clients cannot pass the login wall
  wallPaths: [/identity/accounts/register, /api/accounts/register]
components:
  - name: web
    image: docker.io/vaultwarden/server:1.37.5@sha256:4fe17f415f90087377d37c755e0ea3cf189dcc6794e49cdd2a9adbb4937d9e1f
    port: 8080
    health: {path: /alive}
    resources: {cpu: 50m, memory: 128Mi}
    env:
      ROCKET_PORT: "8080"
      DOMAIN: ${app.url}
      SIGNUPS_ALLOWED: "true"   # safe: registration is behind the login wall
      INVITATIONS_ALLOWED: "false"
      SHOW_PASSWORD_HINT: "false"
      # Vaultwarden's default (WAL, synchronous=NORMAL) loses the last seconds of changes on
      # a hard power loss; FULL syncs every commit (found by the node-loss test).
      DATABASE_CONN_INIT: "PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000; PRAGMA synchronous = FULL;"
    volumes: [{name: data, path: /data, size: 10Gi}]
settings:
  - name: signup_domain
    description: Only allow accounts with email addresses at this domain (empty means any member of the install).
    type: string
    pattern: '^([a-z0-9-]+\.)+[a-z]{2,}$'
    default: ""
    env: {SIGNUPS_DOMAINS_WHITELIST: "${setting.signup_domain}"}
forbidEnv: [ADMIN_TOKEN, SIGNUPS_ALLOWED, SIGNUPS_DOMAINS_WHITELIST]
backup:
  consistency: stop
  require: [data/db.sqlite3]
  # Every restore test runs PRAGMA integrity_check and reports accounts and vault items.
  sqlite:
    - {path: data/db.sqlite3, tables: [users, ciphers]}
actions:
  - name: has_account
    description: Whether at least one Vaultwarden account exists.
    image: docker.io/library/node:24.22.2-alpine3.24@sha256:a34ab6d7f6f4813f4d0c5469d74685604b962fbdbf5793a7bc7b4998ecb867c8
    volumes: [data]
    run: actions/has-account.mjs
    output: {done: {type: boolean}, accounts: {type: number}}
setup:
  - name: first_account
    description: Create your Vaultwarden account (members of this install can create one at any time).
    link: /#/signup
    doneWhen: has_account
notes: |
  Only members of this install can create accounts: registration passes the SlicedBread login wall,
  everything else does not, so Bitwarden apps and extensions work. Give people the account link from
  sb status (it signs them in first). Clients: in the Bitwarden app or extension choose Self-hosted
  and enter the app URL. Data lives on a persistent volume.
